mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Professional Legal Opinion on UBO Chain and Source of Funds

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory multi-list screening against OFAC (SDN), UN Security Council consolidated sanctions, Panama's Lista de Personas Bloqueadas (LAPB), EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions, and all national PEP databases (e.g., Decreto 363 de 2017, Art. 16), processed through specialized AML software with continuous monitoring, risk scoring, and source-of-funds verification for founders, foundation council members, protectors, and ultimate beneficial owners.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Ventanilla Virtual de Trámites (online pre-incorporation clearances via www.registro-publico.gob.pa and the Ventanilla Única de Inversiones at www.vui.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The foundation name must use Latin script only; if the chosen name is in a non-Spanish language, the application must include a certified Spanish transliteration or translation for registration, and the name may not contain only numerals or non-alphabetic characters.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A pending name reservation may be extended for up to two consecutive 30-day periods by filing a renewal request before expiry. If the name is rejected, the applicant shall file a 'recurso de revocación' (reversal petition) before the Dirección de Operaciones del Registro Público within 5 business days; if unsuccessfully answered, an 'recurso de apelación' may be submitted to the Dirección General (Registro Público) within 10 business days; remaining administrative remedies may be pursued before the Sala Tercera de la Corte Suprema de Justicia.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual-office arrangement is permissible only if the licensed registered agent maintains a physical address at which Panamanian process and regulatory notices can actually be served, and the foundation executes a service contract for a physical office address in Panama. For AI/LLM API token providers, low/moderate-risk virtual offices are generally acceptable, but any actual management or operational presence in Panama triggers territorial-source tax and economic substance requirements under Law 41 of 2017.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: The Public Registry conducts unannounced physical inspections of registered offices in approximately 5% of active domestic entities each year, with a slightly higher likelihood if the UBO or transaction patterns are associated with high-risk jurisdictions or financial activity inconsistent with the declared passive holding profile.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law 25 of 12 June 1995 on Private Interest Foundations (as amended by Law 16 of 2016), Articles 3, 5-9 (formation and charter content), 19 (Foundation Council), 27 (Protector), and 30 (registration effects).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Dirección General del Registro Público de Panamá — Mercantile Section (Registro Público de Panamá).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acta de Fundación (Foundation Charter) executed as a public deed before a Panamanian Notary Public, accompanied by a certified copy (testimonio) for registry filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Panama imposes no statutory minimum paid-up capital; however, the Foundation Charter (Law 25, Art. 7) must declare an initial endowment (patrimonio) reasonably sufficient for the foundation's purpose. For an AI/LLM API platform, a notarized declaration of at least USD 10,000 in cash or in-kind intangible assets (software IP, tokenized receivables, API license rights) is recognized practice. No escrow account or bank deposit is legally required; the endowment is an accounting declaration and no forced trustee maintenance applies.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF THE FOUNDATION COUNCIL OF [FOUNDATION NAME]. On [date], at the registered office in Panama City, the Foundation Council lawfully resolved: (1) to accept the Founder's endowment of USD 10,000 or equivalent intangible AI/LLM assets and to record the foundation's books accordingly; (2) to adopt the registered office at the domicile of the Resident Agent, [address], for statutory service purposes; (3) to appoint [Name] as President, [Name] as Secretary, and [Name] as Treasurer, each for a one-year term; (4) to authorize the President and Secretary to execute customer agreements, engage Stripe and USDC payment processors, open bank accounts, and instruct the Protector to supervise. The Council acknowledges the foundation's non-taxable offshore status. Resolved unanimously. Certified by the Secretary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foundation Charter Drafting and Name Availability Review
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Panamanian attorney together with the Public Registry's name-search window (Registro Público de Panamá).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a Panamanian lawyer to draft the Acta de Fundación compliant with Law 25/1995, specifying the foundation name, the Founder, the initial endowment, the Foundation Council, the optional Protector, the registered office at the Resident Agent's address, and the corporate purpose covering ownership of AI/LLM software, hosting of inference API platforms, collection of subscription/token revenues, and holding of payment accounts. Conduct a pre-registration name search at the Public Registry to confirm the foundation's name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered entity.
required_dossiers: Proposed foundation name (three alternatives)
Certified copy of passport of the Founder, Council members and Protector
Proof of residential address and professional references
Preliminary endowment inventory (cash, AI software, API licenses, token assets)
Draft Foundation Charter (Acta de Fundación)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name search is unfavorable, file a written name modification and re-run the search; a rejected endowment declaration is cured by adjusting the charter wording and re-submitting via the same attorney.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Foundation Charter before the Notary Public
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Circuit of Panama (Notaría Pública del Circuito de Panamá).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Founder executes the Foundation Charter before a Panamanian notary in person or by power of attorney. The deed must include the foundation's objects, endowment, council membership, protector powers, procedure for amending the charter, and registered office. The notary will authenticate the act, number it as a public deed, and issue the testimonio (certified first copy) plus two simple copies for registry filing.
required_dossiers: Finalized Foundation Charter text
Original passport or ID of the Founder or notarized power of attorney
Draft attorney legal opinion confirming compliance with Law 25/1995
Notarial fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Notarial discrepancies (e.g., wrong name, capitalization, or endowment figure) are corrected by an addendum of rectification (addendum de corrección) executed before the same notary before any registry filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing and Public Registration at the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Mercantile Section (Petitorio de Inscripción).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deposit the testimonio, two simple copies, and the official fee voucher at the Public Registry's treasury or authorized bank. The Registry's legal reviewer will examine the deed's legality, the endowment clause, the appointment of the Foundation Council, and the registered office. Upon approval, the Foundation is assigned a ficha (record number) and an entry number. Registration creates a separate juridical person under Article 30 of Law 25.
required_dossiers: Certified first copy (testimonio) of the Foundation Charter
Notarial execution record and deed number
Payment receipt of registry fees (USD 280 approx.)
Filing attorney's letter and power of attorney, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues an objection (objeción), the filing attorney submits a written subsanación (correction brief) addressing the identified defect; adverse decisions may be appealed to the Director General of the Public Registry within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Foundation Registry Certificate and Official Extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Certification Section.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the registration entry is completed, request a certificado de inscripción and a certified copy of the registered charter. These documents evidence the PIF's existence, legal capacity, council members, and registered address, and constitute the primary corporate package for opening bank accounts and onboarding payment processors (Stripe and USDC rails).
required_dossiers: Registry entry number (ficha)
Filing receipt and stamped returned copies
Written request for certification on the attorney's letterhead
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certification contains typographical errors, file a correction request at the Certification Section with an explanatory brief and the original certificate; processing averages 2 additional business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Enrollment and Municipal Operation Notice (If Physical Office or Local Sales in Panama)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; Municipalidad de Panamá — Ventanilla SIAV (Sistema de Información de Avisos y Ventanilla Única).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For a PIF that only earns foreign-source digital revenue, no Panamanian income tax registration is required; however, if the Foundation leases an administrative office or contracts with Panamanian clients, apply for RUC using Form FM-01 at DGI and file the Aviso de Operación (annual municipal business license) at the SIAV. Obtain an electronic billing system authorization (facturación electrónica) only for Panama-sourced sales of API access.
required_dossiers: Certificado de inscripción of the Foundation
RUC application Form FM-01
Office lease agreement or registered address declaration
Municipal Aviso de Operación form and fee schedule
Identification documents of the legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI or the municipality requires supplementary documentation, respond within 10 business days; municipal tax assessments may be administratively objected in writing within 15 days of notification under the Municipal Tax Code.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Formation Statutory Governance and Council Organization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Foundation Council, Protector, and Resident Agent (agente residente), overseen by the Public Registry for amendment filings.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the organizational meeting of the Foundation Council; adopt the First Board Resolution; receive the endowment contribution; open corporate bank accounts and crypto-fiat gateways; sign Protector acceptance letters; and formally engage the registered agent. Any subsequent amendment (change of council members, protector, or registered office) must be filed at the Public Registry within 30 days of adoption to avoid surcharges.
required_dossiers: Approved First Board Resolution No. 1
Council member acceptance letters
Protector acceptance and supervision declaration
Bank and payment processor KYC forms (Stripe, USDC on-ramp)
Resident agent engagement agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an amendment is filed late, the Public Registry assesses a surcharge of approximately USD 10 per additional month; the remedy is prompt filing and payment of the graduated penalty, without loss of foundation validity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) — Dirección de Empresas y Derecho Industrial; no sectoral license applies to generative AI/LLM API services under ISIC 6201 because software services are statutorily unregulated in Panama.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación (Municipal Business Operation License) issued by the Municipality of Panama for any administrative office; optional Certificado de Prestador de Servicios Tecnológicos from MICI only if contracting with Panamanian government entities. Neither constitutes a professional license for the AI software activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) — Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt for pure software/AI cloud operations with no physical manufacturing or land modification; Category I simplified Registration applies only if the PIF constructs a physical office exceeding 5,000 m² or deploys a data-center structure. A voluntary self-certification letter registered with MiAMBIENTE is sufficient to demonstrate exemption.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater, VOC, or particulate emission limits are triggered for API platform operations. If any small server room is hosted, comply with: (i) Executive Decree No. 2 of 2009 water-quality standards for cooling systems, if applicable; (ii) Joint Resolution MICI/MiAMBIENTE No. 341 of 2022 on E-waste disposal of IT assets through authorized recyclers; and (iii) technical noise/vibration limits for office equipment per municipal regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá — Certificado de Seguridad (fire-safety clearance) for the office premises, including fire extinguishers, emergency exits, and alarm verification in accordance with NFPA 75 for any small server cabinet; structural load inspection certificate issued by a Panamanian licensed engineer (Sociedad Panameña de Ingenieros y Arquitectos) if server racks exceed floor-load limits; and MITRADEL (Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral) workplace registration and occupational health & safety clearance under Article 335 of the Panamanian Labor Code for any employees in Panama.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas de Panamá; Sede Electrónica portal: https://sedeelectronica.dgi.gob.pa
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign organizer creates the Private Interest Foundation (PIF) through a licensed Panamanian resident agent, filing the foundation charter with the Registro Público de Panamá. Once registered, the PIF obtains a RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) by filing Form RUC before the DGI through the resident agent, accompanied by the registered charter, certificate of registration, and agent authorization. Mandatory RUC/ITBMS registration arises only if the PIF undertakes taxable activities with Panama-source nexus; a PIF that confines its operations to foreign-source AI/LLM API services and foreign counterparties is not obliged to register for Panamanian income tax, but may electively register to claim input VAT recovery on local costs.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election exists in Panamanian tax law. The PIF is subject to territorial income taxation by operation of Law 25 of 1995 and the Código Fiscal; foreign-source revenue of the foundation falls outside Panamanian tax jurisdiction. The foundation may voluntarily elect ITBMS registration and may designate a Panamanian branch or representative for administrative convenience, but such election does not alter territorial classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) – VAT-type consumption tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/.0.00 – no turnover threshold for in-country taxable vendors; any person engaged in taxable Panamanian transactions must register from the first transaction. For pure offshore AI API providers without a Panamanian establishment, no registration is required unless the service is deemed to have Panama-source consumption; zero-rating is available for exporters of services irrespective of volume.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The DGI mandates electronic invoicing through the Sistema de Facturación Electrónica (SFE) for taxpayers designated by annual income band. E-invoices must be issued in DGI-approved XML format, authorized via real-time DGI validation, and carry a QR-linked 'Código de Trazabilidad' before delivery. Certified billing software must expose API endpoints for the DGI's clearance and validation process; non-designated small taxpayers may continue using pre-authorized physical invoice forms.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods qualify for 0% ITBMS when physically exported from Panama and evidenced by a valid customs export declaration. Services, including generative AI and LLM inference API subscriptions, qualify as exports when the service is supplied to a non-resident recipient, the economic benefit is consumed abroad, and all contracting, invoicing and payment activities are carried out with foreign counterparties. The PIF must retain service agreements, invoices, and proof of non-resident user status to substantiate offshore delivery.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación) accepted by the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing actual departure from Panama
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank instrument confirming receipt of foreign currency proceeds
Commercial invoice with ISIC 6201 AI/LLM API service description
Service agreement with non-resident counterparty and proof of beneficial use outside Panama
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Panama operates a dollarized economy without compulsory FX repatriation, but export zero-rating documentation must demonstrate inward remittance within 180 days to satisfy standard audit practice. Fraudulent zero-rating claims trigger retrospective ITBMS assessments at 7% plus daily compounding interest, administrative penalties of up to 150% of the omitted tax, and nullification of the export declarations. Where forged documentation or intent to evade tax is established, the DGI will refer the case to the Ministerio Público for criminal prosecution under the Código Penal carrying imprisonment sanctions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Republic of Panama does not maintain a fiat-issuing central bank. Banking supervision is exercised by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) under Decree-Law 9 of 1998; the Banco Nacional de Panamá (National Bank of Panama) acts as fiscal agent of the Republic; the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) is the financial intelligence unit competent for AML/CFT supervision. The Panamanian Balboa (PAB) is a unit of account pegged 1:1 to the U.S. Dollar, which is full legal tender and circulates freely as the sole physical settlement medium.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama is a fully dollarized open-economy jurisdiction. There are no exchange controls, no convertibility restrictions, no repatriation quotas, and no Central Bank licensing requirement for current or capital account transactions in USD. Profit remittance and capital outbound are unrestricted at the FX level; the only frictions are fiscal and AML-related: (i) Panama-source profit distributions may carry withholding of up to 10% (5% for resident shareholders, 10% for non-residents), while foreign-source AI/LLM API revenue earned by the PIF is exempt under the territorial tax regime when the services are economically performed outside Panama; (ii) the DGI (Dirección General de Ingresos) applies source-of-income doctrine to digital services, so the PIF must preserve documentation proving that the platform sale, inference execution, and customer contracting take place outside Panama; and (iii) SBP-regulated banks must report cash transactions of USD 10,000 or more to the UAF and file suspicious-transaction reports on unusual wire patterns involving non-resident foundations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Panama imposes no statutory obligation to surrender, repatriate, or convert export proceeds, and no mandatory timeline exists for the remittance of foreign revenues. Services exports under ISIC 6201 (AI/LLM inference APIs, generative AI licensing) may be settled freely in USD and retained in the operational accounts of licensed Panamanian commercial banks. The mandatory conversion ratio is therefore 0% with zero surrender window. The PIF should maintain export documentation (customer contracts, usage invoices, cloud provider invoices, API logs summaries) to evidence the foreign-source character of income and to satisfy the bank's annual KYC refresh and any UAF documentary request.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.digital_asset_and_stablecoin_regulatory_: Panama does not grant legal tender status to cryptoassets. The 2022 digital-assets bill (Proyecto de Ley 668) was partially vetoed, and, as of this blueprint, Panama does not operate a fully implemented VASP licensing regime. Settlements in USDC are therefore permissible only as a commercial payment channel and must be converted to USD through a regulated, FATF-compliant exchange or OTC desk before entering the Panamanian banking system; direct stablecoin credits to bank accounts are treated as high-risk and require a complete chain-of-custody file.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.banking_secrecy_and_information_exchange: Panama maintains bank secrecy under Law 52 of 2016 and Tax Information Exchange Agreements; the PIF must obtain a Panamanian tax identification number (RUC) when it generates taxable income and must comply with Common Reporting Standard (CRS) registration if classified as a reporting financial institution, which generally does not apply to a non-financial PIF holding an operational account without investment activity.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Trade Settlement and Commercial LC Account
Classic Current Account for local payroll and statutory maintenance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Private Interest Foundation Annual Franchise Tax Payment and Tax Exemption Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March of each calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers statutory surcharge plus default interest; a continued delinquency of more than 12 months may lead to the legal entity being placed in administrative strike-off status with the Public Registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foundation Annual Registry Attestation and Registered Agent Consent Renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá, Legal Entities Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days after each anniversary of the foundation deed registration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to record the appointed resident agent makes the registry file irregular; unresolved non-compliance can lead to suspension of registry certificates and eventual cancellation of the foundation after administrative dissolution proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Beneficial Ownership Registry / Central Registrar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually no later than the same 31 March deadline, with qualifying beneficiary-rights transfers reported within 30 days after execution.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under the Panamanian preventive due-diligence rules, unexplained omissions are treated as regulatory non-compliance and may incur monetary fines; repeated failure can suspend the foundation’s right to act and lead to compulsory strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent certified audit is compulsory when gross Panamanian-source annual revenues or total assets exceed approximately US$3,000,000; a passive PIF without local commercial activity is exempt from audit and from filing published financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in Panama for public-interest entities; non-listed and small entities may use IFRS for SMEs or Panamanian local GAAP (OCBOA) for internal statutory accounting records.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Because a Private Interest Foundation has no shareholders, the annual confirmation applies to ultimate beneficiary designations and council membership. The resident agent must obtain a signed annual declaration identifying every beneficial owner and any changes of beneficiary rights; any such transfer or replacement must be confirmed in the Registry within 30 days after execution.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficiaries and Protector Appointments
Minute Book of Foundation Council Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$400 – US$850 per annum for a Panama registered agent and registered office for a standard Private Interest Foundation.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not applicable below audit threshold; a certified audit engagement, if triggered, typically ranges from US$3,500 to US$8,500.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (top marginal rate; progressive tiers: 15% on first PAB 1,500,000 of net taxable income, 20% on PAB 1,500,001-3,000,000, 25% above PAB 3,000,000)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial taxation: only Panama-source income is taxable. Foreign-source AI/LLM API platform revenue, token sales, and overseas capital gains are exempt at 0%. Private Interest Foundations under Ley 25 de 1995 pay a fixed annual foundation fee of PAB 350 and effectively incur zero corporate income tax on non-Panama business activity. No net-worth tax, no municipal income tax, and no capital gains tax on foreign portfolio assets.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 105 - Declaracion Jurada de Impuesto Sobre la Renta; filed electronically through the DGI e-Tax / SICAR portal (Direccion General de Ingresos) using the foundation's RUC and registered digital signature.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; complemented by mandatory advance income tax prepayments (Anticipo) paid in equal installments during the fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months following the close of the fiscal year; calendar-year foundations must file by 31 March of the following year, with payment of the final balance due on the same date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: RUC taxpayer identification number, legal name of the Private Interest Foundation, fiscal period, and registered address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident foundations must appoint a Panamanian resident agent and obtain an RUC before any filing; the agent attests to the foundation's active registry status.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part II, Line 20 - Panama-Source Gross Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income derived from activities performed or sources located within Panamanian territory.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only domestic AI/LLM API revenue, if any; a pure offshore platform with no Panamanian customers reports zero here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income derived from extraterritorial sources, exempt under Article 693 of the Codigo Fiscal.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report global LLM API token revenue, subscription fees, and API usage fees invoiced outside Panama; keep a sworn geographic revenue breakdown for audit support.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable costs, expenses, and deductions attributable to Panama-source taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign operating costs attributable to foreign-source revenue are not allocated to Panama-source income; maintain a separate internal cost ledger.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part V, Line 52 - Net Taxable Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Panama-source gross income minus allowable deductions; the base to which progressive 15/20/25% rates apply.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an offshore AI API platform, report zero or a nominal Panama-source amount; the return must still be timely filed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part V, Line 60 - Final Tax Payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed income tax after applying progressive rates, prepayments, and creditable withholding taxes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If foreign-source income exemption applies fully, the amount payable is zero; a zero-value filed return preserves the exemption claim.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a monthly surcharge of 5% of the tax due per month or fraction thereof, capped at 50%, plus statutory default interest accruing daily from the original due date. Administrative fines range from PAB 10 to PAB 500 per unfiled return. Willful omission of Panama-source revenue can result in fraud reassessments of 100%-200% of the evaded tax and criminal referral.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Private Interest Foundation Flat Fee (Tasa Unica Anual) under Ley 25 de 1995, Article 38; paid via the DGI e-Tax portal, Banco Nacional de Panama, or through the registered resident agent.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, synchronized with the foundation's registration anniversary.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within three months after the anniversary of registration in the Registry of Private Interest Foundations; a foundation registered in January must settle by 31 March.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unique registration number of the Private Interest Foundation in the Public Registry.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The resident agent retrieves the registry number and submits payment on behalf of the non-resident council.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation that the foundation is active, has a designated resident agent, and maintains a registered address in Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident founders must keep the resident agent appointment current to avoid late fees and registry sanctions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fixed annual public fee of PAB 350.00, irrespective of income, assets, or activity level.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment is mandatory even if the foundation has zero Panama-source income and no employees in Panama.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment accrues a monthly surcharge of 2% up to a maximum of 50% of the fee, the DGI will withhold 'Paz y Salvo' tax clearance, and persistent non-payment exposes the foundation to registry cancellation, restriction of bank account operation, and loss of the territorial exemption.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% withholding on dividends or profit distributions made from Panama-source net taxable profits. Distributions sourced from exempt foreign-source AI/LLM API revenue carry 0% Panama withholding under the territorial regime. Bearer-share or untraceable shareholder structures are subject to additional complementary tax of 5%-10% on undistributed Panama-source profits.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA benefits, the foundation must (i) obtain a Panama Tax Residency Certificate ('Certificado de Residencia Fiscal') from the DGI by petitioning with the RUC, constitutional documents, resident-agent certificate, and board resolution; (ii) deliver the TRC and Panama DTA relief form to the foreign payer before the distribution date; and (iii) apply the reduced rate under the applicable treaty. Panama's enforceable DTAs include Mexico, Luxembourg, Singapore, France, Spain, Portugal, Qatar, Italy, and the United Kingdom, and Panama applies the OECD Multilateral Instrument to align treaty provisions with BEPS standards. Reduced dividend rates generally range from 5% to 10%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to a non-resident for intellectual property used or exploited within Panama are Panama-source and subject to a 15% statutory withholding on gross consideration; treaty rates typically reduce this to 5%-10%. Interest paid by a Panamanian borrower to a non-resident lender is generally subject to 5% withholding unless exempt as international banking financing; treaty rates reduce interest to 0%-5%. Outbound payments for foreign-source licensing of the AI/LLM model or platform infrastructure generate no Panama withholding tax.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: PAB 3,000,000 (equivalent USD) of annual gross taxable income or related-party transactions triggers mandatory transfer pricing documentation, including the Local File (Informe Local), Master File (Informe Maestro), and the annual Transfer Pricing Informative Return (Declaracion Informativa de Precios de Transferencia / Formulario 1873). Below-threshold taxpayers must retain contemporaneous benchmarking documentation and are subject to DGI audit requests.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama has not enacted Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations for Private Interest Foundations; however, the territorial exemption is strictly source-based and requires demonstrable non-Panama management and commercial activity. A PIF holding AI/LLM API platform contracts must maintain board minutes, commercial agreements, bank accounts, and evidence that decisions and revenue-producing activities occur abroad. Management exercised from Panama, or use of the foundation as a pure conduit, invites DGI re-characterization, foreign CFC attribution, CRS/FATCA exposure, and loss of the 0% effective rate.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of Panama-source AI/LLM API revenue, use of fictitious foreign invoices, inflated offshore deductions, or filing a Form 105 that conceals local digital commerce activity and Panamanian customers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties under Codigo Fiscal Articles 753, 764 and 780, and Codigo Penal Article 281: fines of 100%-200% of the evaded tax, criminal imprisonment of 2 to 5 years, retroactive elimination of territorial tax benefits, and automatic suspension of tax clearance certificates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The court may pierce the foundation veil where the council used the entity to defraud; council members are jointly and severally liable for civil restitution of the evaded amount and may face preventive detention, travel bans, and penal sentences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the PIF as a bare shell to conceal beneficial ownership of LLM API platform revenue, failing to maintain accounting records, neglecting the annual PAB 350 flat fee, or lacking any legitimate commercial substance and resident-agent compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Registry cancellation, forced liquidation of foundation assets, fines of PAB 1,000 to PAB 5,000 for registry and AML breaches, and retroactive disallowance of the foreign-source exemption resulting in full 25% corporate income tax reassessment plus surcharges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under Ley 25 de 1995 and general civil fraud principles, the foundation veil is pierced for fraud or abuse; directors and officers exposed to damages, personal asset attachment, court-imposed injunctions, and travel restrictions during DGI and Public Registry investigations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering / AML Violation - Ley 23 de 2015
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving USDC or other cryptocurrency payments for AI/LLM API services without implementing KYC and beneficial-ownership controls, operating an unregistered virtual-asset business when categorized as a VASP, or using the PIF to layer proceeds of fraudulent API billing schemes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines by the Unidad de Analisis Financiero of up to PAB 1,000,000, criminal imprisonment of 5 to 12 years, forfeiture of contaminated assets, and listing on the Beneficial Ownership Registry sanctions register.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: AML investigations permit outright piercing of the foundation structure; council members may face seizure of personal funds, preventive detention, a 10-year travel prohibition during the investigation, and criminal liability as co-authors of laundering.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Misstatement and Documentation Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file Formulario 1873, late or absent Local File and Master File, or charging non-arm's-length prices to related offshore entities, including overpriced token royalties or API service fees that erode the Panamanian taxable base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI transfer pricing adjustment with a penalty of 10% of the corrected amount, monthly default interest on the reassessed tax, fines of PAB 500 per missing document, and extension of the statute of limitations where the omission is fraudulent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign knowingly distorted transfer pricing returns are jointly liable for the assessed differences and penalties; aggravated cases carry criminal complicity exposure under tax fraud provisions.
